contract.description: Hand-authored finite-step PageRank and finite-sweep label propagation goldens for already-extracted tiny projections. Physical edges are stored directed arcs; LPA symmetrizes them. These supplement, not replace, stationary references.
contract.bounds: 1..6 distinct u64 node IDs; <=12 physical edges with distinct u64 IDs; 1..100 iterations/sweeps. PageRank edges require explicit finite nonnegative binary64-compatible weights; integer weights <=2^53. LPA edges have no weights. PageRank seed_ids is a nonempty unique subset of the already-admitted nodes, used only to validate personalization, not to extract scope. Personalization IDs must be scoped seeds; unlisted nodes have zero teleport mass.
contract.ordering: Node visits and returned rows ascend by numeric ID, regardless of input order. Edges ascend by ID. PageRank is synchronous; LPA updates immediately within ascending-ID sweeps. Traces include only full steps/sweeps, including the full converging step/sweep.
contract.reference: PageRank interprets binary64 weights, damping, tolerance and positive personalization masses with Fraction.from_float, then computes exact rational steps from r=p. Each exported finite score and L1 residual is compared independently to the hand-reasoned expected value within the stated absolute tolerances. This is not bitwise equivalence with an iterative f64 runtime, nor a stationary solution used to infer iterations.
contract.interruption: synthetic_vertex_update_budget is null or 0..600; one unit per candidate vertex update, including isolates. It models interruption only, not VLite work accounting. A partial step/sweep is discarded. No full step/sweep means null scores/residual or assignments. A full final step/sweep can converge even at an exact cap/budget boundary; otherwise the cap is incomplete. Reasons are null, iteration_limit or synthetic_interruption.
contract.exclusions: No TTL/scope extraction, authorization, storage, real engine budgets/deadlines, allocator, production qualification, weighted LPA or numerical parity claims.

cases.name: pr_uniform_dangling_two_steps_capped
cases.purpose: With p=(1/2,1/2), d=1/2 and 1->2, the synchronous first step is (3/8,5/8), L1=1/4; second is (13/32,19/32), L1=1/16. Tolerance 0.05 does not certify the capped second step.

cases.name: pr_uniform_converges_exactly_on_cap
cases.purpose: The same two full steps converge on the cap because final L1=1/16 equals tolerance. Budget four permits exactly two full two-vertex steps, not an interruption.

cases.name: pr_parallel_loop_synchronous
cases.purpose: Node 1 sends 1/4 to itself and 3/4 to 2 through two weighted parallel arcs; 2 returns to 1. At d=1/2 the first vector is (9/16,7/16), second (69/128,59/128). Updating node 2 with new node-1 rank would instead give 59/128 in the FIRST step, exposing in-place errors.

cases.name: pr_personalized_dangling_two_steps
cases.purpose: Mass seven on seed 1 normalizes to p=(1,0). For 1->2 and d=1/2, r1=(1/2,1/2) with L1=1, r2=(3/4,1/4) with L1=1/2; dangling redistribution is to p, not uniform.

cases.name: pr_zero_arcs_personalized_converging_first_step
cases.purpose: Zero outgoing arc and negative-zero loop leave both nodes dangling. Normalized masses 1:3 give p=(1/4,3/4), preserved in the first full step even with binary64 damping 0.85. Residual zero certifies convergence on cap one.

cases.name: pr_interrupted_before_first_full_step
cases.purpose: One vertex update computes candidate rank 1=1/2, but cannot finish the two-vertex first step. Initial p must not leak as returned scores; residual and scores are absent.

cases.name: pr_interrupted_partial_second_step
cases.purpose: Three updates complete r1=(1/2,1/2), then compute candidate node 1=3/4. Discard that partial second step and return only r1 and its residual 1.

cases.name: lpa_tie_keep_collapsed_capped
cases.purpose: Visits 1->4, 2->3; node 3 keeps tied current 3 and node 4 keeps tied current 4 despite smaller 3. Duplicate/reversed 3-4 edges collapse, loops vanish, isolate 5 stays. One changed sweep is incomplete; raw labels 4 and 3 canonicalize to 1 and 2.

cases.name: lpa_tie_keep_converges_on_cap
cases.purpose: Same collapsed graph: sweep two changes no labels, certifying convergence exactly on cap two and synthetic budget ten. An already stable-looking first partition alone was not convergence.

cases.name: lpa_smallest_tie_immediate_three_sweeps
cases.purpose: Node 1 picks smallest tied neighbor label 3 rather than 4; node 2 picks 5. Immediate updates make node 3 retain 3, node 4 pick 3, node 5 adopt majority 3. First labels (3,5,3,3,3), second all 3 after node 2 changes, third unchanged certifies convergence.

cases.name: lpa_interrupted_before_first_full_sweep
cases.purpose: Budget one updates node 1 to label 3 but cannot finish the first sweep. Neither initial nor partial assignments may be returned.

cases.name: lpa_partial_second_sweep_rolls_back_changed_label
cases.purpose: Budget seven completes first labels (3,5,3,3,3), then visits nodes 1 and 2 in sweep two; node 2 changes to 3. Discard the partial sweep: node 2 must still return label 5/community 2, not merge into community 1.
